sydney-au.name: Sydney
sydney-au.tagline: Harbour city of beaches, ferries, and sandstone headlands
sydney-au.general: Sydney wraps a world-famous harbour with surf beaches, coastal walks, ferry rides, and national-park headlands. It is the natural starting point for east-coast journeys, Blue Mountains day trips, and food-led city stays.
activities: Ride the ferry to Manly at sunset
Explore The Rocks and Circular Quay
Take a day trip into the Blue Mountains
tips: Use an Opal or contactless card for ferries and trains
Book harbour restaurants ahead on weekends
Beach conditions change quickly; swim between the flags

photos.caption: Sydney Harbour Bridge from Circular Quay

melbourne-au.name: Melbourne
melbourne-au.tagline: Laneway culture, galleries, trams, and Great Ocean Road access
melbourne-au.general: Melbourne is Australia's culture capital: laneway cafes, street art, live music, major galleries, and easy tram travel. It also anchors road trips to the Great Ocean Road, Phillip Island, the Yarra Valley, and the Grampians.
activities: Follow a laneway coffee and street-art walk
Ride the tram to St Kilda Pier
Visit the NGV and Federation Square
Start a Great Ocean Road drive
tips: Weather can swing in a day; carry layers
The free tram zone covers central sights
Reserve popular restaurants before Friday and Saturday nights

Melbourne Skyline from Rialto Crop - Nov 2008

brisbane-au.name: Brisbane
brisbane-au.tagline: Subtropical river city between islands and rainforest hinterland
brisbane-au.general: Brisbane follows the bends of the Brisbane River with galleries, riverside dining, bike paths, and easy access to Moreton Bay islands. It is a practical base for Lamington, the Scenic Rim, and south-east Queensland beaches.
activities: Walk South Bank and the riverfront
tips: Summer storms can be sudden
Use go card or contactless payment on public transport
Book island ferries during school holidays

perth-au.name: Perth
perth-au.tagline: Indian Ocean beaches, Swan River sunsets, and Rottnest escapes
perth-au.general: Perth pairs Indian Ocean beaches with a relaxed riverfront city, Kings Park views, Fremantle heritage, and short ferry rides to Rottnest Island. It is the west-coast launch point for wine regions, coral coast drives, and the Cape to Cape Track.
activities: Explore Fremantle's markets and heritage streets
Ride a ferry to Rottnest Island
tips: Distances in Western Australia are large; plan fuel stops
Book Rottnest ferries and bikes early in summer
A hat and sun protection are essential year-round

adelaide-au.name: Adelaide
adelaide-au.tagline: Parkland city for wine valleys, beaches, and festivals
adelaide-au.general: Adelaide is a compact city ringed by parklands and close to beaches, the Adelaide Hills, Barossa, McLaren Vale, and Kangaroo Island. Its markets, festivals, and wine access make it an easy South Australia base.
activities: Taste wine in the Adelaide Hills
Plan a Kangaroo Island side trip
tips: Festival season fills rooms quickly
Wine tours are easiest with a designated driver or guide
Summer heat can be extreme inland

canberra-au.name: Canberra
canberra-au.tagline: Planned capital of museums, lake loops, and bushland ridges
canberra-au.general: Canberra is Australia's planned capital, built around Lake Burley Griffin and framed by bushland hills. National museums, parliament, galleries, cycling paths, and nearby Namadgi National Park make it a thoughtful inland stop.
activities: Visit Parliament House and the National Gallery
Climb Mount Ainslie for the city axis view
tips: Winter mornings are cold and frosty
Many national institutions are free
A car helps for nature reserves and suburban dining

hobart-au.name: Hobart
hobart-au.tagline: Tasmanian harbour capital below kunanyi / Mount Wellington
hobart-au.general: Hobart sits between the Derwent River and kunanyi / Mount Wellington, with Georgian streets, Salamanca markets, ferries, MONA, and access to southern Tasmania's wild coast and convict heritage.
activities: Climb or drive to kunanyi / Mount Wellington
Visit Port Arthur as a day trip
tips: Mountain weather is colder than the waterfront
Book Bruny Island and Port Arthur tours ahead
Saturday market mornings are busiest

photos.caption: Aurora Australis (icebreaker) berthed in Hobart under a rainbow

darwin-au.name: Darwin
darwin-au.tagline: Top End gateway for markets, sunsets, Kakadu, and Litchfield
darwin-au.general: Darwin is the tropical Top End capital, known for waterfront sunsets, markets, World War II history, and access to Kakadu, Litchfield, and Arnhem Land touring.
activities: Visit the Museum and Art Gallery of the Northern Territory
Use Darwin as a Kakadu launch point
tips: The dry season from May to September is most comfortable
Observe crocodile warning signs around waterways
Many remote trips require permits or guided access

cairns-au.name: Cairns
cairns-au.tagline: Reef and rainforest base in tropical Far North Queensland
cairns-au.general: Cairns is the main base for Great Barrier Reef trips, Wet Tropics rainforest, Kuranda rail journeys, and Daintree excursions. The city is compact, tour-friendly, and built around tropical outdoor travel.
activities: Take a reef snorkel or dive day trip
tips: Reef boats book out in school holidays
Marine stinger season usually runs November to May
Summer is humid and wet; carry rain protection

gold-coast-au.name: Gold Coast
gold-coast-au.tagline: Surf beaches, skyline stays, and rainforest hinterland trails
gold-coast-au.general: The Gold Coast mixes surf beaches and high-rise resorts with rainforest hinterland parks, waterfalls, and family attractions. It is a bright, easy stop between Brisbane and northern New South Wales.
tips: Swim only between flags
Weekend traffic builds around theme parks
Hinterland roads can be misty after rain

alice-springs-au.name: Alice Springs
alice-springs-au.tagline: Red Centre town for desert ranges and Larapinta Trail access
alice-springs-au.general: Alice Springs is the practical hub of Australia's Red Centre, backed by the MacDonnell Ranges and the Larapinta Trail. It works best for self-drive desert trips, Aboriginal art, and outback landscapes.
activities: Walk sections of the Larapinta Trail
Visit the Alice Springs Desert Park
tips: Carry far more water than you expect to need
Avoid exposed hikes in midday heat
Remote-road fuel and supplies need planning

photos.caption: Northern Territory, Alice Springs 4992, Australia (2024-01-13-13-53-58 UMBRA-08)

auckland-nz.name: Auckland
auckland-nz.tagline: Harbour city of volcanic cones, islands, and Pacific food
auckland-nz.general: Auckland spreads across twin harbours, volcanic cones, island ferries, black-sand surf beaches, and diverse Pacific dining. It is New Zealand's biggest gateway and a flexible start for North Island journeys.
activities: Climb Mount Eden for crater and skyline views
Take a ferry to Waiheke Island
Walk the waterfront and Wynyard Quarter
tips: Traffic can be slow at peak times
Book Waiheke ferries and restaurants on sunny weekends
Weather changes quickly; carry a light shell

wellington-nz.name: Wellington
wellington-nz.tagline: Compact capital of harbour hills, cafes, museums, and film craft
wellington-nz.general: Wellington compresses parliament, museums, coffee, craft beer, hillside walks, and a working harbour into a walkable capital. It is also the ferry link between the North and South Islands.
activities: Ride the cable car to the Botanic Garden
tips: Wind is part of the experience; pack a shell
Cook Strait ferries need advance booking with vehicles
Central Wellington is easy without a car

christchurch-nz.name: Christchurch
christchurch-nz.tagline: Garden city rebuilt with creativity and Canterbury access
christchurch-nz.general: Christchurch blends botanic gardens, new architecture, markets, street art, and easy access to Banks Peninsula, Arthur's Pass, and the Canterbury high country.
activities: Punt or walk along the Avon
Day-trip to Akaroa or Arthur's Pass
tips: Layer for cool evenings even in summer
Book rental cars early in peak South Island season
Road trips west can be affected by alpine weather

queenstown-nz.name: Queenstown
queenstown-nz.tagline: Alpine lake base for adventure, wine, and Great Walks
queenstown-nz.general: Queenstown sits on Lake Wakatipu beneath the Remarkables, with jet boats, gondola views, wineries, ski fields, and access to Routeburn, Fiordland, and Mount Aspiring landscapes.
activities: Use town as a Great Walks base
tips: Accommodation prices spike in ski season and summer
Book Milford and Routeburn logistics early
Mountain weather changes fast

rotorua-nz.name: Rotorua
rotorua-nz.tagline: Geothermal lakes, Maori culture, and forest trails
rotorua-nz.general: Rotorua is known for geothermal valleys, steaming lakes, Maori cultural experiences, and mountain-bike trails in Whakarewarewa Forest. It is a strong North Island nature and culture stop.
activities: Experience a cultural performance and hangi
tips: Geothermal steam has a sulphur smell around town
Book cultural evenings ahead
Forest trails drain well but can be muddy after rain

dunedin-nz.name: Dunedin
dunedin-nz.tagline: Southern heritage city with wildlife-rich Otago Peninsula
dunedin-nz.general: Dunedin combines Scottish-influenced streets, student energy, railway architecture, surf beaches, and Otago Peninsula wildlife. It is a rewarding southern city stop before the Catlins or Central Otago.
activities: Look for albatross and penguins on Otago Peninsula
tips: Wildlife viewing is best with low-impact guided operators
Coastal weather can be cool and windy
Respect closed beach areas during nesting season

nelson-nz.name: Nelson
nelson-nz.tagline: Sunny arts town near Abel Tasman beaches and alpine parks
nelson-nz.general: Nelson is a sunny South Island base for galleries, markets, wineries, Abel Tasman beaches, and inland alpine parks. It works well for slower coastal travel and Great Walk logistics.
activities: Browse Saturday market and local galleries
Taste wine around Moutere or Mapua
Walk to the Centre of New Zealand viewpoint
tips: Summer accommodation fills early
Book Abel Tasman water taxis in advance
A car helps connect beaches, wineries, and trailheads

wanaka-nz.name: Wanaka
wanaka-nz.tagline: Lakeside mountain town for day hikes and Mount Aspiring access
wanaka-nz.general: Wanaka is a calmer alpine-lake base than Queenstown, with day hikes, ski fields, bike trails, and access to Mount Aspiring National Park. It suits outdoors-focused road trips through Otago.
activities: Walk Mount Iron or Roys Peak
tips: Roys Peak is exposed; start early and carry water
Winter roads may require chains
Trailhead parking can fill before sunrise

broome-au.name: Broome
broome-au.tagline: Kimberley beach town of red cliffs, pearls, and sunset camels
broome-au.general: Broome sits on the Indian Ocean edge of the Kimberley, known for Cable Beach sunsets, pearling history, red pindan cliffs, dinosaur footprints, and long dry-season road trips into remote north-west Australia.
activities: Use Broome as a Kimberley road-trip base
tips: The dry season is busiest and most comfortable
Book tours and 4WD hire early
Check tide times for coastal sights

exmouth-au.name: Exmouth
exmouth-au.tagline: Ningaloo Reef base for whale sharks, beaches, and canyon country
exmouth-au.general: Exmouth is the main northern gateway to Ningaloo Reef and Cape Range National Park, pairing coral snorkel beaches with red limestone gorges and seasonal whale shark tours.
activities: Join a whale shark or manta ray tour
tips: Marine wildlife seasons vary by month
Carry water and shade for Cape Range walks
Book reef tours well ahead in peak season

margaret-river-au.name: Margaret River
margaret-river-au.tagline: Wine, surf, karri forest, caves, and the Cape to Cape coast
margaret-river-au.general: Margaret River is a south-west base for vineyards, surf breaks, limestone caves, tall forest, local produce, and the Cape to Cape Track between two Indian Ocean lighthouses.
activities: Visit Lake Cave or Mammoth Cave
Walk a Cape to Cape section
tips: A car is useful for wineries and beaches
Book cellar doors and restaurants on weekends
Spring brings wildflowers and cooler walking weather

photos.caption: 2016 Margaret River Australia. Memorial chapel St John the theologian

airlie-beach-au.name: Airlie Beach
airlie-beach-au.tagline: Whitsundays harbour town for island sailing and reef flights
airlie-beach-au.general: Airlie Beach is the mainland hub for the Whitsunday Islands, with marina departures for sailing trips, Whitehaven Beach, reef flights, and relaxed lagoon-side evenings.
tips: Book sailing trips ahead in school holidays
Marine stinger suits are common in warmer months
Cyclone season can disrupt plans

katoomba-au.name: Katoomba
katoomba-au.tagline: Blue Mountains town for sandstone lookouts and canyon walks
katoomba-au.general: Katoomba is the best-known Blue Mountains base, close to the Three Sisters, cliff-edge walks, waterfalls, heritage guesthouses, and multi-day tracks heading toward Jenolan Caves.
activities: See the Three Sisters from Echo Point
Walk the Prince Henry Cliff Walk
tips: Weekend trains from Sydney can be busy
Cliff weather can turn cold and misty
Carry a headlamp for longer valley walks

townsville-au.name: Townsville
townsville-au.tagline: Dry tropics city for Magnetic Island and reef-country access
townsville-au.general: Townsville combines a dry tropical waterfront with Castle Hill views, museums, reef gateways, and ferries to Magnetic Island's beaches, koalas, forts, and granite headlands.
activities: Ride the ferry to Magnetic Island
Visit the Museum of Tropical Queensland
tips: Magnetic Island buses connect key bays
Summer heat is intense
Check marine stinger advice before swimming

launceston-au.name: Launceston
launceston-au.tagline: Northern Tasmania base for Cataract Gorge and Tamar Valley
launceston-au.general: Launceston is a compact northern Tasmanian city near Cataract Gorge, heritage streets, Tamar Valley vineyards, and road routes to Cradle Mountain and the east coast.
activities: Taste wine in the Tamar Valley
Use the city as a Cradle Mountain gateway
tips: Winter mornings are cold
A car helps connect vineyards and parks
Book Cradle Mountain shuttles and accommodation ahead

port-douglas-au.name: Port Douglas
port-douglas-au.tagline: Tropical resort town between reef boats and Daintree rainforest
port-douglas-au.general: Port Douglas is a relaxed Far North Queensland base with Four Mile Beach, marina reef departures, Sunday markets, and easy access to Mossman Gorge and the Daintree.
activities: Join a Great Barrier Reef cruise
tips: Reef trips are weather dependent
Book restaurants in peak dry season
Respect crocodile and stinger warnings
